_note: Phase 0 proof numbers only, never a personal reading. null = not measured yet, and scripts/rebuild_gate.py counts an unmeasured target as missed unless the owner waived it (waived_targets, his words).
image_note: Artifact Registry repository cloud-run-source-deploy holds 115.1 MB after the first build and 185.9 MB with two images; a clean-up policy keeps the 2 newest (under the free 0.5 GB). Measured 2026-10-19.
upload_note: gcloud meta list-files-for-upload: 84 files, all engine code (61 in services/, 12 in api/, the seven root modules, Dockerfile, requirements-engine.txt and the two ignore files); the source zip was 687 KiB. 2026-10-19.
cold_start_note: Revision health-engine-00004 (commit 7291d6c): two natural cold starts, 20+ minutes apart, sent through the Worker as the phone sends them, both answered (9.13 s and 11.02 s). The owner stopped the timing there. Revision 5 (commit 2ff03cf) precompiles the engine's code into the image to cut the import time (4.5-5.5 s on Cloud Run against 1.3 s on the PC); it is deployed and not timed.
warm_note: From the owner's PC, each request on a new TLS connection: 440 ms straight to Cloud Run and 427 ms through the Worker, so the Worker's extra hop is lost in the noise (measured -13 ms).

waived_targets.cold_start_median_s: the owner, 2026-10-19: "the cold start timing doesnt matter" and "if it's not free it's not going to change the outcome of switching". Measured median of the two timed starts: 10.08 s against the 10 s target.

oura_probe.what: one read of yesterday's daily_readiness from Cloud Run with the stored access token; no refresh

garmin_probe.what: one login (email and password) and one read of yesterday's daily summary from Cloud Run, with the owner's OK; the tokens can be stored

free_tier_projection.pattern: the owner's: one sync a day at the first morning open plus one retry, ten cold starts a day, each sync at twice the 77 s the Streamlit chain took; a cold start billed at the worst timed one, 11.02 s (scripts/rebuild_p0_measure.py project --start-s 11.02)
free_tier_projection.egress_out_of_belgium: 0.08 GB a month, about $0.01 (Premium tier, no free amount in Europe)
free_tier_projection.google_meters_2h_sample: 33.4 billed instance-seconds and 12 requests on 2026-10-19 (two starts, the Garmin and Oura probes, the checks)

cold_start_revision_2_note: Revision health-engine-00002 (commit 6dd2fcf, compressed): the first request after the engine slept, sent through the Worker at 09:43:55 UTC, was REFUSED by Google (HTTP 500, 'The request was aborted because there was no available instance'; the instance started 5 s later). The Worker answered 503 after 11.3 s. Fixed: the Worker retries Google's refusals (1, 2, 4, 8 s), the engine answers JSON for every error so the two cannot be confused, and the copy from Supabase fetches 4 tables at a time (5.9 s -> 1.5 s from the PC). The timing script had read the 503 as 'Worker not ready' and timed a direct request that met a half-started engine (3.0 s); that sample is void.
cold_start_revision_3_note: Revision health-engine-00003 (commit 5f772c4) never started: Supabase answered one request of its copy with 401 PGRST303 'JWT issued at future' (a moment of clock difference inside Supabase; the same requests worked minutes later). Fixed in commit 7291d6c: that one error is tried again after 0.5, 1 and 2 s.
cold_start_revision_1_note: Revision health-engine-00001 (commit 84c88c6, before Supabase compression): one natural cold start, 10.66 s direct (imports 3.82 s, config 0.08 s, cache rebuild 4.98 s); the deploy-time start logged imports 2.61 s and cache rebuild 6.02 s.
